groups.contract: Canonical native timestamp admits all signed microseconds but conversion has endpoint limits
groups.disposition: Complete343-line pinned body personally read including property fixtures, not run. from_micros_since_unix_epoch accepts all i64, preserving legitimate pre-epoch values. to_duration_since_unix_epoch negates negative micros before u64 cast; MIN cannot be negated in i64, so this native representable endpoint panics with overflow checks or wraps in unchecked release before producing duration. to_system_time calls that conversion, and platform checked_add/sub further enforce representability. from_system_time explicitly rejects every pre-epoch time despite signed timestamp range, not a symmetric conversion guarantee. Duration->Timestamp checks u128 micros narrows via try_into before publication. Display calls fallible chrono/RFC3339 conversion then unwrap; native i64 endpoints can exceed Chrono date range. These are actual native API/representation strengthening dependencies at first-party timestamp formatting/conversion ports, not a current wall-clock/player-timeline failure. Preserve pre-epoch signed support and declared platform precision; do not globally conflate strategic calendar clock with Unix timestamp.

groups.contract: Timestamp arithmetic prepares checked result before assignment; native Duration conversion remains dependency
groups.disposition: time_duration_since uses checked signed subtraction then canonical TimeDuration and nonnegative duration conversion. checked_add/sub TimeDuration use checked i64 arithmetic; operator Add/Sub deliberately unwrap and assignment evaluates that result before replacing retained timestamp, so arithmetic rejection leaves old value except panic unwinding policy. checked_add/sub_duration first calls TimeDuration::from_duration; huge stdDuration admission/error policy of that constructor is not proven by the checked name here and remains separate native dependency. Current first-party callers must choose checked native operation and representable scheduling outcome where their contract promises no panic, retaining actual signed/zero semantics. Existing source fixtures cover some arithmetic and current-system-time, not every native endpoint; no new tests or execution.
